headline: The Kelton sits inside American Fork's FrontRunner Station-Area / TOD district. Refined with the city's General Plan plus a verified entitlement/records pass, the supply picture splits cleanly by horizon. NEAR-TERM (0-3 yr): competitive attached-housing supply is ALREADY DELIVERING immediately around the subject - D.R. Horton's 'Edgewater' townhomes (sales office 351 S 1110 W, multiple phases under construction, first phase completed Dec-2025) and Woodside's 'Meadowbrook / Regency at Meadowbrook' townhomes (853 W 560 S, ~10 phases, ~half completed in 2025) - both for-SALE townhomes but city-classified 'Multifamily,' with a 123-unit 'Meadowbrook TOD Phase 4' multifamily building now under review. LONGER-TERM (3-7+ yr): the dominant future apartment threat is a ~116-acre band of vacant, largely developer-held land inside American Fork's ~444-acre TOD future-land-use area wrapped around the subject - anchored by BACH Investments LLC's 15.3-ac TOD parcel (BACH = Bach Homes of Draper, a prolific apartment builder: 350-700 units/yr, the 285-unit Bach Homes AF Apartments, the 338-unit Elevate/Lake City Row) plus Silverado Partners (~13 ac), OCAP AF TOD LLC (~6 ac), AF I-15 LLC (~7 ac) and ~71 ac of RA-zoned-but-TOD-planned family land. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the TOD zoning that permits the city's highest density (60+ du/ac) rides on the American Fork Station Area Plan, which was still only a PROPOSED (Planning-Commission-recommended, not yet Council-adopted) General Plan Amendment as of Aug 2025 - the pipeline is real but not fully in force, and NO specific site plan or development agreement is on file for BACH's parcel. CORRECTIONS to the base analysis (development-priced land value did NOT equal apartment entitlement): Blue Spring (General Plan Residential Very-Low Density; part of its land, serial 13:041:0080, is being conveyed to UTA/UDOT for FrontRunner double-track right-of-way), the Lehi 'PC' parcels (base 3 du/ac + Environmentally-Sensitive/greenbelt, apartments only via discretionary Area Plan), and Windy City (Very-Low-Density Res-Ag) are down-ranked to Low - they are NOT near-term apartment sites. Bridges at Fox Hollow is detached single-family (87 lots), not multifamily. Net: near-term competition is townhomes-for-sale already in the ground; the large rental-apartment threat is a credible but entitlement-dependent, developer-held TOD land bank, not shovel-ready.

ranking.rationale: The single most credible future apartment site: 15.3 vacant acres zoned TOD, ~0.4 mi NW, owned by BACH INVESTMENTS LLC. Verified: BACH = an affiliate of Bach Homes (Draper, UT; principal Shon Rindlisbacher), a self-described land-development/apartment-construction firm that adds 350-700 apartment units/yr and already built the 285-unit Bach Homes American Fork Apartments (2021) and the 338-unit Elevate at 620 - clear capacity and intent to develop a TOD site at 60+ du/ac. BUT no site plan, preliminary plat, or development agreement for parcel 13:038:0068 survived verification, and the TOD framework itself (Station Area Plan GPA) was still only PC-recommended/not-adopted as of Aug 2025. So: highest ceiling, real developer, no filed project yet -> a 3-7 yr threat, not imminent. Sources: Utah County land records; bachhomes.com; AF PC records.

The ~98-ac band abutting the subject (0.23 mi). Its AF-side ~70 acres is zoned RA-1/RA-5 today but designated Transit-Oriented Development in American Fork's General Plan - a rezone-in-waiting to high density, and part of a ~116-ac vacant TOD land bank around the Kelton also held by Silverado Partners LLC (~13 ac), OCAP AF TOD LLC (~6 ac) and AF I-15 LLC (~7 ac). Verified nuance: ownership is MIXED, not a single individual assemblage - control serial 13:041:0044 is individually held (Allred family) while 13:041:0080 in this cluster is actually BLUE SPRING PROPERTIES LLC, part of which was quit-claimed to UTA (+a UDOT easement) in Apr-2026 for FrontRunner double-track right-of-way. No rezone, plat, or master plan for these specific parcels survived verification. So: large TOD-planned land bank = a genuine long-horizon high-density threat, but raw, multi-owner, partly being consumed by transit infrastructure - not an entitled project. Sources: AF General Plan (Land_Use GIS); Utah County AbstractReverse/SerialByEntry.

RH Johnson Construction's parcel at 518 W 200 S is one of three parcels (13:042:0028/0062/0063, ~7.2 ac) the American Fork Planning Commission recommended 6-0 on Jan 8, 2025 to rezone from Planned Industrial (PI-1) to TOD - so it is entitlement-ADVANCING, contradicting a 'vacant/unentitled' read. But city staff stated it was a staff-initiated MAP CLEANUP 'not due to any proposed project'; one parcel is listed for sale; and staff flagged that development is 'challenged' by required right-of-way dedication and the FrontRunner double-tracking. By-right TOD density if adopted, but small and constraint-laden. Source: AF PC minutes 01/08/2025.

~37 vacant acres ~0.6 mi N (Lehi), zoned A-5 today but designated 'Commercial / Residential' in Lehi's General Plan - so residential (incl. attached) is plan-supported and a rezone is plausible over time. No filed application verified. A medium-horizon watch, not near-term. Source: Lehi General Plan (GIS).

Blue Spring Properties' ~23 ac, ~0.45 mi S. DOWN-RANKED from the base 'Medium': American Fork's General Plan designates it Residential VERY-LOW Density (large-lot single-family), not apartments, and no development plan, rezone, or listing survived verification. High assessed value reflects hot-market low-density lot value, not apartment entitlement. (Blue Spring also owns TOD-area land near the station, serial 13:041:0080, part of which is being taken by UTA/UDOT for transit ROW.) Not an apartment threat as planned. Source: AF General Plan; Utah County records.

The Lehi 'Planned Community' parcels (~19 ac, ~0.9 mi SW). DOWN-RANKED from base 'Medium-Unknown': the Lehi PC zone sets a base residential density of only 3 du/acre, and apartments (12 du/ac) or townhomes (8 du/ac) are legally possible ONLY as higher-density pods via discretionary Area Plan approval, offset by lower-density pods; the parcels are also mapped 'Environmentally Sensitive Area' and carry a ~$18k/ac (greenbelt/Farmland-Assessment) value. No active Area Plan for these parcels was found. A long-horizon, discretionary rezone play near Utah Lake - low near-term threat. Source: Lehi Development Code Ch.6; Lehi General Plan.

Windy City Development's ~51 ac, ~1.0 mi SW, zoned Lehi A-5 and designated 'Very-Low-Density Residential Agriculture' in Lehi's General Plan. No annexation, rezone, plat, or listing survived verification (status unresolved, but nothing supports an apartment use). Large developer-held holding, but the plan is large-lot ag-residential - not competitive apartment supply. Source: Lehi General Plan.
Harbor Enterprises' ~8.6 ac RA-5, ~0.56 mi S; AF General Plan Residential Low Density. Small, SF-planned, no verified activity. Not an apartment threat.
Walking the Wire's ~17 ac, zoned R1-12000 and AF General Plan Residential Low Density - a single-family subdivision, not apartments. No verified development activity. Confirmed low.
Harbor View Development's ~19 ac ~1.8 mi S is largely AF 'Shoreline Protection' (non-developable lakeshore) with a low-density PR-2.0 remnant; sliver-shaped. Not an apartment site.
